claims.claim_ar: التفات: الانتقال البلاغي من صيغة تقرير/توكيد قائلة («قُلْ لَنْ يُصِيبَنَا إِلَّا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنَا») إلى خطاب مباشر موجه للمؤمنين بأمر («فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ»)، أي تحويل السياق من إخبار إلى مخاطبة لتحريك التوكل الفعلي.
claims.claim_en: Iltifat (shift of address/style): the verse shifts from a declarative assurance about divine decree to a direct imperative addressed to the believers ("فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ"), changing the illocutionary force from report to address to prompt practical reliance.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited Zamakhshari passage states the phenomenon as "الأمر في معنى الخبر" and gives examples; it supports a shift/force-change analysis but does not explicitly name it 'التفات' for this exact verse, so the mapping is inferential.

claims.claim_ar: نكتة بلاغية: استخدام الأمر بمعنى الخبر كأداة بلاغية لخلق 'نكْتَة' — نقطة تأثيرية/مؤثرة تبرز التناقض الظاهري بين الخطر المحتمل وقطع العجز بالإيمان والتوكل.
claims.claim_en: Naktah (rhetorical punch/point): the use of an imperative-as-report (as discussed by Zamakhshari) produces a rhetorical 'punch' that highlights and intensifies the assurance of divine decree and the consequent call to trust.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source explicitly uses the term 'نكتة' about similar constructions; applying it to this verse is plausible but inferred rather than directly stated for this exact ayah.

warnings: Source material provided is from Zamakhshari only and does not systematically use the modern technical labels (e.g., 'التفات', 'نكتة') for every verse; some device identifications are inferential based on the cited commentary passages.

source_quote_ar entries are exact substrings from the supplied chunks and are used as supporting evidence; those chunks discuss analogous constructions (e.g., 'الأمر في معنى الخبر') rather than this verse word-for-word.
